papers.title: MPPI-Generic: A CUDA Library for Stochastic Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a new C++/CUDA library for GPU-accelerated stochastic optimization called MPPI-Generic. It provides implementations of Model Predictive Path Integral control, Tube-Model Predictive Path Integral Control, and Robust Model Predictive Path Integral Control, and allows for these algorithms to be used across many pre-existing dynamics models and cost functions. Furthermore, researchers can create their own dynamics models or cost functions following our API definitions without needing to change the actual Model Predictive Path Integral Control code. Finally, we compare computational performance to other popular implementations of Model Predictive Path Integral Control over a variety of GPUs to show the real-time capabilities our library can allow for. Library code can be found at: https://acdslab.github.io/mppi-generic-website/ .

papers.title: BF16 Component-Product Emulation of FP32 and FP64 GEMM on Intel AMX
papers.abstract: Modern CPUs increasingly integrate high-throughput matrix engines optimized for low-precision AI workloads, while many scientific computing applications still rely on FP32 and FP64 GEMM to meet their numerical accuracy requirements. This paper presents a method that combines BF16 matrix products on Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) to emulate real square FP32 and FP64 GEMM. For FP32 GEMM, each element in both input matrices is decomposed into three BF16 components, and six selected component products are evaluated to target FP32-level accuracy comparable to oneMKL SGEMM. For FP64 inputs within the supported BF16 exponent range, the method uses a simplified fixed six-slice Ozaki decomposition. Each retained BF16 product is first produced in FP32, then widened and accumulated in FP64. Four product-count settings retain 6, 10, 15, or 21 component products, exposing the accuracy-performance tradeoff relative to oneMKL DGEMM. The FP32 schedule reuses component data and retains partial sums in AMX tiles. AMX-FP32 outperforms oneMKL SGEMM at tested orders $N\ge4096$ on 64 threads and also achieves gains for smaller matrices at lower thread counts. AMX-FP64 variants retaining fewer component products can outperform oneMKL DGEMM at sufficiently large orders; more products improve accuracy at additional cost.

papers.title: Pauli Decomposition by Character Theory: A Memory-Bounded Algorithm for Qubits and Qudits
papers.abstract: Pauli decomposition of an $n$-qubit operator is expensive if each of the $4^n$ Pauli strings is treated as an unstructured object. Labeling those strings by the configuration space $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ makes them displacement operators $X^{\otimes x}Z^{\otimes z}$ on the computational space: shifts by~$x$ and multiplications by characters $Z^{\otimes z}$ in the computational basis. That labeling organizes the operator into $2^n$ fibers of length $2^n$, one per shift~$x$, each collecting the computational-basis amplitudes that hop by~$x$. Expanding each fiber function in the character basis of $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ --- a length-$2^n$ Walsh--Hadamard transform --- recovers the Pauli coefficients at total cost $O(n\cdot4^n)$. The same fiber / shift--character picture extends to $(\mathbb{Z}_p)^n$ (Heisenberg--Weyl qudits). \texttt{paulikit} is a memory-bounded realization for qubits: for matrix-sparse inputs, peak memory need not densify to a full $2^n\times2^n$ operator. Performance is checked on a stated low-end GNU/Linux platform for a coupled-oscillator sweep beyond a billion Pauli terms.
